subject: SLA carveout request for streaming latency & sustained throughput
messages:
From: Kate Moran <kate@brighthealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T15:04:12Z
Subject: Pilot request — streaming SLA expectations

Neha,

Thanks for the product walk-through yesterday. As we scope the pilot with Redwood we need clarity on how streaming endpoints will be contractually measured. Our security and reliability teams are comfortable with your hosted offering generally, but for clinical routing we need guaranteed time-to-first-token (TTFT) and a sustained tokens/sec expectation for streaming calls.

Specifically: can you confirm whether the standard SLA (TTFT x ms / uptime %) applies to streaming the same way it does to sync generation? If not, will Redwood accept a limited carveout for the pilot that documents a measured TTFT window and a sustained tokens/sec target (we plan to exercise streams continuously for 30–60 minutes in a throughput test harness)?

We attached our SLO requirements document. We have an internal deadline to sign the pilot by 12/3. Could we get a proposed exception/wording and a short technical note on how measurement/monitoring would work?

Thanks — Kate
Kate Moran

BrightHealth Inc.

Kate / Neha — here are practical constraints and a recommended proposal based on the model family you referenced on yesterday's call (gpt-large-rl):

1) TTFT (time-to-first-token) measurement notes:
   - TTFT is sensitive to cold-starts, KV cache priming, and prompt prefix length. We measure TTFT at the edge (ingress) to first byte emitted by the serving runtime.
   - For dedicated pools with pinned warm instances and typical clinical prompt sizes (<= 1k tokens), realistic median TTFT is ~80–140 ms. P95 sits around 300–500 ms under bursty concurrency unless we provision additional warm capacity.

2) Streaming sustained throughput (tokens/sec) expectations:
   - Sustained tokens/sec per connection depends on model variant and CPU/GPU packing. For the pilot configuration we suggest a conservative guarantee: 35 tokens/sec sustained per stream (measured as a 1-minute moving average) with the caveat that simultaneous concurrency > X will trigger autoscale/fallback.
   - If BrightHealth wants a higher sustained rate (50+ tokens/sec) we will need a reserved burst pool and concurrency limits in contract.

3) Operational controls and measurement:
   - Monitoring: we will instrument TTFT, tokens/sec, and per-request fallbacks; we will share a dashboard and an API to fetch raw samples for the agreed test windows.
   - Fallbacks: policy will be documented (e.g., fall back to scaled-quant model, region failover). Fallbacks will be considered a non-availability event unless they materially change output quality.

Proposed pilot SLA (technical):
   - Term: 90 days
   - TTFT: median target 120 ms; P95 target <= 450 ms (measured at ingress over 30-day rolling window)
   - Sustained streaming throughput: 35 tokens/sec per stream (1-min moving avg), measured across the pilot harness during designated test windows (specified in contract)
   - Measurement windows: production telemetry + two 60-minute validated run windows performed jointly (we provide harness instructions).

I attached a short pilot-sla-proposal PDF that includes graphs showing expected behavior at different concurrency levels. If that looks good we can convert it into carveout language for the contract.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao

Hi all — thanks Aditya for the clear technical proposal. From a commercial standpoint here's how we'd encode this:

- Pilot carveout clause (90 days): we will include an addendum to the Master Services Agreement that enumerates the pilot-specific TTFT and sustained tokens/sec targets, the exact measurement methodology, and the test windows.
- Credits / remedies: given the pilot nature we prefer a remedial path (engineering work + joint mitigation schedule) and a limited credit (capped percentage of pilot fees) if metrics are missed for X consecutive measurement windows.
- Concurrency / reserved capacity: the carveout will specify reserved concurrency and a burst pool size; BrightHealth needs to confirm expected peak concurrency so we can size the pool.
- Rollback & termination: if output quality materially degrades during fallback we will provide an escape clause for BrightHealth with a defined notice period.

Neha — please put together the initial addendum draft. Rafael, looping legal to review and add necessary limits. Kate, can you confirm expected peak concurrent streams and whether the 60-minute validated run windows are acceptable?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Kate Moran <kate@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:16:05Z
Subject: Re: Pilot request — streaming SLA expectations (legal redlines)

Folks — reviewed the proposed language. High level: we can support a 90-day pilot carveout, subject to the following redlines (summary):

1) Scope & measurement: require an agreed test harness and measurement spec (we have to reference the Drive doc). The measurement will be performed by Redwood using the agreed harness, with BrightHealth allowed an observer role and the ability to export raw samples.
2) Remedies cap: for the pilot we will cap credits to the greater of (a) 25% of pilot fees or (b) $25k, whichever is lower. We will not agree to uncapped refunds.
3) Termination: either party can terminate the pilot for material SLA breaches with 14 days' notice; remediation plan required before credits are payable.
4) Data & compliance: ensure the carveout references existing data handling and SOC2 obligations — fallbacks that alter model execution paths must be logged and auditable.

I attached an annotated redline (sla-pilot-redline.docx). Once Kate confirms concurrency numbers, operations will convert Aditya's tech bullets into contractual measurement language and we can circulate the draft addendum.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-pilot-redline.docx
